asset.title: Before you move Supabase Auth email to Loops
asset.content:
Subject: Before you move Supabase Auth email to Loops
Preview text: Compare route coverage before configuring templates and a verified sending domain.

Match your sending route to Auth coverage

Hi there,

For Supabase Auth, the decision starts with coverage. Loops is an email sending platform that can take over Auth email through either SMTP or the Send Email Hook.

SMTP covers confirm signup, magic link, invite, change email and reset password. The hook covers all Send Email Hook action types, including security notifications.

Both routes use Loops transactional emails and require configured templates and a verified Loops sending domain. The hook also uses a Supabase Edge Function, with one Loops template for each Auth type you configure.

Changing the sending route does not address Supabase’s separate Auth email rate-limit setting. Treat that as a separate Supabase configuration decision.

Loops’ Supabase docs compare the two routes, their supported email types and their setup, so you can choose based on the coverage your app requires.

Read the Supabase docs → https://loops.so/docs/integrations/supabase

- Loops

asset_metadata.body:

SMTP covers confirm signup, magic link, invite, change email and reset password. The hook covers all Send Email Hook action types, including security notifications.

asset_metadata.single_idea: Choose the Loops route by Auth email coverage: use the Send Email Hook for all hook action types, including security notifications, or SMTP for the five documented core types.

selected_brief.selection_reason: A Supabase team moving Auth email needs to know which documented Loops route covers the email types it plans to send. Coverage and setup requirements are more useful at consideration stage than a broad platform pitch.

value_case.reader_benefit: A Supabase team can choose a sending route that matches its required Auth email coverage: the Send Email Hook covers all hook action types, including security notifications, while SMTP covers five named Auth email types.
value_case.mechanism: The Send Email Hook uses a Supabase Edge Function and one Loops template for each configured Auth email type. The SMTP route covers confirm signup, magic link, invite, change email and reset password. Sending through Loops also requires a verified Loops sending domain.
decision_conditions: The Send Email Hook requires a Supabase Edge Function and a Loops template for each configured Auth email type.
SMTP is limited to confirm signup, magic link, invite, change email and reset password.
A verified Loops sending domain is required.

claim_conditions: Keep the argument limited to Supabase.
Present the Send Email Hook and SMTP as distinct routes with different coverage.
State the verified-domain requirement as a prerequisite, not as an outcome.
A Loops sending domain must be added and verified before auth email will send (E42).
The SPF, DKIM, MX and DMARC records Loops supplies must be copied into DNS; Loops recommends a sending subdomain such as mail.yourcompany.com (E251, E261).
The Send Email Hook route requires a Supabase Edge Function and one Loops template per auth action type (E1).
The SMTP route requires at least the Confirm signup and Magic Link templates, with Confirm signup's variables also present in Magic Link (E395, E387).
The post-signup onboarding sequence requires the separate Supabase contact-sync setup; the Send Email Hook covers auth email only (E37, E380).

The Clerk branch is only partly served: Loops syncs Clerk users and can run onboarding workflows (E274, E276), but Clerk keeps sending its own authentication emails (E285), so a Clerk team cannot move auth email itself to Loops. On the Supabase branch, SMTP covers five auth types only (E225, E387), an auth type without a Loops template falls back to Supabase's own sender (E230), and unmapped action types are silently skipped in the documented Edge Function (E41). Regional sending, which the audience definition already marks unverified, is not established by the selected evidence, and nothing in the selected evidence speaks to Supabase's own auth-email rate limit.

Loops becomes the sender for these auth email types, but the selected evidence establishes nothing about the auth platform's own auth-email rate limit, which P3 reports continues to apply; on the SMTP route only five types are covered (E225, E387) and an untemplated type falls back to Supabase's own sender (E230).

The documented material names Loops-side prerequisites and failure modes (required templates, verified domain, fallback to Supabase's sender, silently skipped unmapped action types) but establishes nothing about the reported 500 and 535 errors inside Supabase's own SMTP configuration or about recovering after reverting; the report is single-source and undat…
selected_brief.target_audience: A Supabase or Clerk app team moving auth and onboarding email off the platform's built-in defaults before launch
selected_brief.job: Help the reader choose whether the Send Email Hook or SMTP route matches the Supabase Auth email types they need to send.
selected_brief.single_idea: Choose the Loops route by Auth email coverage: use the Send Email Hook for all hook action types, including security notifications, or SMTP for the five documented core types.
selected_brief.mechanism: Loops documents two separate Supabase routes. The hook route uses an Edge Function and one Loops template per configured Auth type; SMTP covers confirm signup, magic link, invite, change email and reset password. Either route requires a verified Loops sending domain.
selected_brief.belief_shift: Before: Loops is another possible provider for Supabase Auth email. After: the reader understands the concrete coverage difference and prerequisites well enough to choose which route deserves evaluation.
must_not_say: Do not claim that Loops removes, raises or bypasses Supabase's own auth-email rate limit or resolves HTTP 429 errors.
Do not claim that Loops addresses how Supabase communicates that its built-in sender is for testing.
Do not claim that Loops identifies or configures Supabase's auth-email rate-limit setting or any self-hosted environment variable.
Do not claim that upgrading a Supabase plan changes its built-in email limit.
Do not extend this auth-email proposition to Clerk; the Loops Clerk integration does not take over Clerk authentication emails.
Do not say SMTP covers every Supabase Auth email type; its documented coverage is confirm signup, magic link, invite, change email and reset password.
Do not promise delivery, inbox placement, launch readiness, faster setup, fewer errors or any customer result.
Do not imply the recipient has already encountered throttling, attempted a migration, visited documentation or spoken with Loops.
Do not introduce discounts, urgency, customer proof, onboarding workflows, pricing or unrelated integrations.

Keep the connection route attached to its cited source. A native or prebuilt integration and a custom HTTP/webhook endpoint are separate setup paths unless the source explicitly equates them. A platform name alone establishes neither manual endpoint configuration nor a no-setup connector. Keep unknown setup requirements unknown; do not mix the steps or benefits of those paths.
selected_brief.objection: The reader may not know whether the broader hook coverage is worth its additional Edge Function and per-template setup compared with SMTP.
selected_brief.next_step_decision: Choose whether to evaluate the Send Email Hook or SMTP based on required Auth email coverage and setup conditions.
selected_brief.next_step_value: The documentation shows the two supported Supabase Auth routes, their coverage and the setup involved, including the hook's Edge Function and template model.
selected_brief.next_step_limit: Reading the documentation does not establish whether Supabase's own auth-email rate limit will still apply in the reader's environment.
selected_brief.subject_strategy: Name the practical Supabase decision—Send Email Hook or SMTP—without implying an incident, urgency or guaranteed fix.
